sourceInformation.source: H.E.R.O. (1984), created by John Van Ryzin and published by Activision
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer (WebGPU with WebGL2 compatibility); Rapier 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; WebRTC; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Procedural 3D cel shading with three-band light, ink outlines, faceted caves and industrial rescue equipment
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip keyframe tracks, with procedural flight, rescue and effects animation
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated sector music (10% by default), sound effects, jetpack hum and Animalese-style formant gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub ghost races for 1–4; standalone local-tab ghost races and two-player direct WebRTC pairing
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 with native WebGPU and WebGL2 visual checks; scripted full-campaign playthrough without cheats; standard gamepad emulation; native multitouch emulation; offline/live Web Audio; actual BroadcastChannel and WebRTC; official Hub 2-player, adverse 4-player and host-leave scenarios. Real hardware input feel and Internet NAT reachability: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: none; native model knowledge for H.E.R.O.; supplied AI Hub integration files read directly

testingFeedback: 10 issues were caught across automated checks, visual review and controller audit; all were fixed. The development issue ledger records each one.
3 were game breaking during development: fourth-copy native GPU startup, stale GPU recovery callbacks, and browser gestures cancelling touch flight. All are fixed.
The complete three-sector physical-input AI playthrough without cheats: it uses the flight, laser and timed-charge systems, opens every bulkhead, rescues all six miners and reaches victory.
Native headless WebGPU screenshots were blank despite valid game state. The same scenes were checked visually through the WebGPURenderer WebGL2 backend instead.
engineFeedback: Three.js native AnimationMixer clips and cel-shaded node materials make procedural characters and caves feel cohesive.

Four concurrent software WebGPU copies exposed native pipeline errors; renderer disposal then exposed stale cache callbacks. Recovery now retires the failed device and rebuilds a fresh scene through WebGL2.
The data-driven rescue campaign, jetpack controls, destructible walls, controller UI and ghost-race lifecycle.
Recovering cleanly from asynchronous GPU initialization failure while keeping physics and game state valid.
Make failed GPU pipeline compilation reject cleanly, and remove resource disposal listeners when a renderer is disposed.
promptFeedback: The source-inspired vertical slice, controller-first UX and explicit attract-mode, procedural-audio and testing requirements give the game a clear identity.
No internet research is allowed while a live integration URL must be followed; I treated reading the supplied protocol files as integration work.
Combining a polished three-sector campaign, procedural audiovisuals, multiple input styles and real multiplayer in one self-contained HTML file.
Separate required protocol documentation from the no-research rule, and clarify whether standalone multiplayer requires relay hosting for restrictive networks.

aiHub.name: H.E.R.O. Blast Shift
aiHub.description: Strap on a pocket rotor and descend into three ink-lined mines. Blast bulkheads, outfly cave creatures and bring six stranded miners home, solo or against ghost pilots.
aiHub.controls: A/D move, Space/W fly, mouse aim + fire (J laser), E/right-click charge, Q scanner, Esc pause; pad: left stick, Cross/A fly, R2/RT laser, R1/RB charge, Triangle/Y scan; assisted dual-stick touch.
